draft.title: Consumer Affairs Victoria
card: Consumer Affairs Victoria (CAV) is a Victorian government body. It deals with the rights of consumers, tenants and renters.
It gives information for free. It explains the law to consumers, traders, landlords and tenants, so people know their rights and duties before a dispute grows.
It also helps people settle disputes for free, such as a faulty product or a rental bond dispute. It contacts the other party and tries to help the two sides reach agreement.
CAV is not a court. It does not hear evidence and make a binding ruling. If a dispute is not settled, a person can take it to another body, such as VCAT.
draft.remember: CAV is a free government service that informs and helps settle disputes, but it does not rule on them.

a.q: Which statement best describes the role of Consumer Affairs Victoria in a dispute?
opts: It helps the parties reach agreement, at no cost
It hears evidence and makes a binding order
It represents the consumer as their lawyer in court
It charges a fee based on the size of the claim
a.why: CAV helps parties settle disputes and does not charge for this. It is not a court, so it does not hear evidence and make a binding order. That is the most tempting wrong option.
a.clue: CAV helps with agreement. It is not a court.

b.q: Priya rents a flat in Geelong. Her landlord refuses to refund her bond. She asks CAV for help, but the dispute is not settled. What is true of CAV's role?
opts: It can contact the landlord, but cannot force a ruling
It can order the landlord to repay the bond
It must take the dispute to court for her
It can only give her information, not contact the landlord
b.why: CAV helps settle tenancy disputes for free, which includes contacting the other party. It cannot make a binding ruling, so an unsettled dispute may go to another body such as VCAT. It does more than give information, so the last option is wrong.
b.clue: CAV helps settle disputes, but it does not decide them.

a.best: It helps the parties reach agreement, at no cost

b.best: It can contact the landlord, but cannot force a ruling

b.q: Jack buys a fridge from a store in Bendigo. It breaks, and the store refuses a refund. He asks CAV for help, but the dispute is not settled. What is true of CAV's role?
opts: It can contact the store, but cannot make a binding ruling
It can order the store to refund him, as a tribunal would
It can act as his lawyer if he sues the store in court
It can give him information, but cannot contact the store
b.why: CAV helps settle consumer disputes for free, which includes contacting the other party. It does not make a binding ruling, so an unsettled dispute can go to another body such as VCAT. Ordering a refund is the tempting option, but that is what a tribunal or court does, not CAV.
b.clue: Recall what Jack can do next if CAV cannot settle it.
